newsitem.title: USA: Fate of W. Va., Trust Fund rests with legislature.
newsitem.headline: Fate of W. Va., Trust Fund rests with legislature.

text.p: West Virginia's $4 billion pension trust fund will be dissolved and the money transferred unless the legislature acts by April 12 to reconfigure it, the fund's executive director, Craig Slaughter, said Friday.

"Unless the Legislature does something, the trust fund will have to shut down and transfer the money somewhere else. I really don't know where," Slaughter said. "They have been working to correct the situation and I'm confident they will do something."

West Virginia's constitution prohibits the investment of public money in equities. In 1995, the legislature attempted to circumvent the law by creating the West Virginia Trust Fund as an independent entity to invest workers compensation and state pension fund money in stocks and other securities.
The state attorney general challenged the measure, saying the investments could only be authorized by a constitutional amendment and not by legislative fiat.

A Kanawha County judge agreed, and last week the state Supreme Court upheld that court's ruling that the fund was created illegally. The state Supreme Court ordered that the fund be dissolved within 30 days, by April 27.
The Legislature must act before its April 12 adjournment in order to prevent the dissolution, Slaughter said.
Already, the House has approved a bill that basically recreates the fund, minus the authorization to make equity investments. A similar proposal is pending in the Senate.
"They (the supreme court justices) were very clear that we can't invest in stocks," Slaughter said.
But beyond that, the ruling left it up to the legislature to decide what to do with the fund, he said.
Lawmakers are also working on a proposed constitutional amendment authorizing equity investments, which could go before voters in the fall.
Because of the legal dispute, the Trust Fund has never held any equities. It is invested entirely in fixed-income instruments, including U.S. Treasuries and high-grade corporate bonds.
West Virginia is the only state that still bans equity investment of public money, a prohibition that dates back to the stock market collapse that triggered the Depression.
